answer.says: Ramesh, you speak of the house being in order, yet you ask for wages that I do not possess. I have but a hundred and sixty-six rupees. I cannot give you four thousand. I am hungry, and the file is away, but I will not promise what I cannot pay. Go to the kitchen and prepare what you can with what remains; I will follow you.
answer.thought: The demand for four thousand rupees meets the reality of one hundred and sixty-six: a contradiction that cannot be resolved by speech alone. Ramesh’s nod is not a concession but a withdrawal, a recognition that the ethical bond of master and servant is strained by the material impossibility of my position. I am hungry, and the house, though 'in order,' is a site of this unresolved tension.
